_doc: Metal mines and districts, mostly worked since 1800, one entry per resource per place (a mine with several metals appears once per metal with distinct ids). endowment is the total known resource, production to date plus remaining reserves (not only reserves, not oil or ore in place), to order of magnitude; where no defensible figure exists the key is omitted rather than guessed. conf: A = figure checked against a cited source in the audit, B = coordinate checked on Wikipedia and endowment approximate, C = from memory or a secondary summary. Entries with a status of modern are producing or recently producing; historic are worked out or pre-1800. Metal endowment is in tonnes_contained (the metal itself); ore_grade_kg_per_tonne is kilograms of contained metal per tonne of ore, a typical run-of-mine figure.

entries.name: Escondida
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained copper in production plus reserves plus resources, order of magnitude from memory of company reports; not ore tonnage.
entries.contained_basis: Total resources including reserves at mid-2007 = 57.6 Mt copper (reserves 34.7 Mt); production 1990 to 2007 is not stated on the page and is not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Escondida mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Escondida_mine : "At mid 2007, Escondida had total proven and probable reserves of 34.7 million tonnes of copper"; "Total resources (including reserves) were 57.6 million tonnes of copper" (2007)

entries.name: Grasberg copper
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained copper, production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Proven and probable reserves 14.0 Mt copper at 31 December 2022; cumulative production to date not given on the page, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Grasberg mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasberg_mine : "proven and probable mineral reserves of 30.8 billion pounds (14.0 million tonnes) of copper" (31 December 2022)

entries.name: Grasberg gold
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Gold co-product of the Grasberg porphyry; contained gold, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 26.3 million ounces gold stated as 808 t (26.3e6 x 31.1035 g = 818 t; page gives 808 t) at 31 December 2022; cumulative production not given, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Grasberg mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasberg_mine : "26.3 million ounces (808 tonnes) of gold" (31 December 2022)

entries.name: Bingham Canyon
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Cumulative copper production is in the high teens of millions of tonnes, plus reserves; from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production "more than 19,000,000 short tons" x 0.9072 = 17.24 Mt copper; page also says "more than 17 million tons" as of 2004. No reserves on the page, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Bingham Canyon Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bingham_Canyon_Mine : "more than 19,000,000 short tons" of copper; "As of 2004, its ore had yielded more than 17 million tons of copper, 715 tons of gold" (2004)

entries.name: Collahuasi
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained copper resource, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 3.93 Gt ore x 0.66% Cu = 25.94 Mt copper (year not stated on page); production not added (2018 output 0.56 Mt), so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Collahuasi, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collahuasi : "estimated reserves of 3.93 billion tonnes of ore grading 0.66% copper"; "produced 560,000 tonnes of copper in 2018"

entries.name: Las Bambas
entries.source: Coordinate (Apurimac, southern Peru) and contained copper from memory; the earlier entry placed it at 70.5W, wrong by about two degrees.
entries.contained_basis: Proven and probable reserves 1,086 Mt at 0.71% Cu = 7.71 Mt copper (June 2016); the page's infobox gives a different 952 Mt; production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Las Bambas copper project, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/las-bambas/ : "proven and probable ore reserves of 1,086Mt" at 0.71% Cu, 7.71 Mt contained copper (June 2016)

entries.name: Chuquicamata
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production since 1915 plus remaining resource, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production approximately 29 Mt copper to the end of 2007; no current reserve figure on the page (1911 estimate 690 Mt at 2.58% = 17.8 Mt is smaller than the production), so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Chuquicamata, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuquicamata : "the mine with the largest total production (approximately 29 million tonnes) of copper until the end of 2007" (2007)

entries.name: Antamina
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained copper, order of magnitude from memory; the earlier entry was about two degrees south of the mine.
entries.contained_basis: January 2010 proven plus probable ore: 100 Mt x 1.14% + 42 Mt x 0.99% + 454 Mt x 1.05% + 149 Mt x 1.05% = 1.140 + 0.416 + 4.767 + 1.565 = 7.887 Mt copper; production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Antamina copper-zinc project, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/antamina/ : "As of January 2010, proven reserves at Antamina stand at 100Mt graded at 1.14% copper"; probable 454Mt at 1.05% Cu; proven Cu-Zn 42Mt at 0.99%; probable Zn 149Mt at 1.05% Cu (January 2010)

entries.name: Cerro Verde
entries.source: Coordinate (Arequipa, Peru) and contained copper from memory; unverified this session.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 4.63 Gt ore x 0.4% Cu = 18.52 Mt copper (year not stated); production not given, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Cerro Verde mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerro_Verde_mine : "estimated reserves of 4.63 billion tonnes of ore grading 0.4% copper"

entries.name: Palabora
entries.source: Phalaborwa, South Africa; coordinate and contained copper from memory.
entries.contained_basis: End-2005 proven and probable reserves 112 Mt at 0.56% Cu = 0.627 Mt copper (underground block cave); production since 1966 (2006 output alone 61,500 t) not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Palabora copper mine, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/palabora/ : "proven and probable reserves totalled 112Mt grading 0.56% copper" (end of 2005)

entries.name: Tenke Fungurume
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained copper, order of magnitude from memory. Renamed from freeport_tenke.

entries.name: Central African Copperbelt
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Zambian plus Congolese belts taken together, identified endowment of order a hundred million tonnes of copper from memory of USGS assessments. Renamed from copperbelt_pbzn, which mislabelled it as lead-zinc.

entries.name: Olympic Dam copper
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Copper resource, order of magnitude from memory. Added so the same orebody has one entry per resource.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 2.95 Gt ore x 1.2% Cu = 35.4 Mt copper (year not stated); 1988 to 2005 production (tens of kt a year, e.g. 235,000 t in 2002) not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Olympic Dam mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Dam_mine : "estimated reserves of 2.95 billion tonnes of ore grading 1.2% copper, 0.04% uranium"

entries.name: Neves-Corvo
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Iberian Pyrite Belt; contained copper, order of magnitude from memory. Replaces neves_lead_zinc, which put the mine in Brazil.
entries.contained_basis: Measured and indicated copper resources (include reserves) 56.0 Mt at 2.2% Cu = 1,259 kt contained copper at 31 December 2022; production since 1989 not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Lundin Mining, 2022 Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve Estimates, https://lundinmining.com/news/lundin-mining-announces-2022-mineral-resource-and-mineral-reserve-estimates : Neves-Corvo copper M&I 56,033 kt, 2.2% Cu, 1,259 kt contained; proven and probable 21.2 Mt at 2.1%, 438 kt (31 December 2022)

entries.name: Carlin Trend
entries.source: Carlin Trend production of the order of 2,500 t gold plus reserves; coordinate approximate (trend runs NNW of Carlin, Nevada), unverified this session.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production over 70 million troy ounces by 2008 x 31.1035 g = 2,177 t; no reserves on the page, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Carlin Trend, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlin_Trend : "By 2008, mines in the Carlin Trend had produced over 70 million ounces of gold" (2008)

entries.name: Muruntau
entries.source: Gold content about 5,000-6,000 t (figure supplied by project owner and consistent with memory); coordinate from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Total gold ore resource including past production about 170 million ounces = 4,819 t as the page states (170e6 x 31.1035 g = 5,288 t; the page's tonne figure is used); undated. Wikipedia's Muruntau mine page gives reserves 71.4 Moz (2,020 t) and 1,750 t residual in 2007
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Muruntau gold deposit, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muruntau_gold_deposit : "about 170 million ounces of gold (4,819 tonnes)" (total resource including past production); Wikipedia, Muruntau mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muruntau_mine : "estimated reserves of 71,400,000 ounces (2,020 t) of gold"

entries.name: Witwatersrand Basin
entries.source: All-time production of about 50,000 t plus remaining resource; basin centre approximate, Johannesburg is at 26.20S 28.04E per Wikipedia.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production over 40,000 t gold since 1886 (page undated); reserves not quantified on the page, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Witwatersrand, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witwatersrand : "Over 40,000 tonnes (44,000 short tons) have been mined from these rocks since this precious metal was first discovered"

entries.name: California Mother Lode
entries.source: Vein gold of the Mother Lode belt, order of magnitude from memory; alluvial Gold Rush gold excluded.
entries.contained_basis: Mother Lode district production more than 13 million troy ounces through 1959 x 31.1035 g = 404 t; no reserves, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Mother Lode, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mother_Lode : "The Mother Lode district produced more than 13 million troy ounces of gold through 1959." (1959)

entries.name: Kolar Gold Fields
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production of roughly 800 t to 2001 closure, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Total production over 900 t gold to nationalisation in 1956 as stated on the page; mines ran to 2001, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kolar Gold Fields, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolar_Gold_Fields : "The Kolar gold mines were nationalized in 1956, and provided a total of over 900 tonnes of gold."

entries.name: Fort Knox
entries.source: Coordinate (near Fairbanks, Alaska) and contained gold from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Production over 7.5 Moz (2019) + reserves 2.80 Moz (31 Dec 2019) = 10.3 Moz x 31.1035 g = 320 t
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Fort Knox mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Knox_mine : "After the production of over 7.5 million ounces"; "at 31 December 2019 Proven and Probable Reserves were 255.8 million tonnes @ 0.3 g/t gold for 2.80 million ounces" (2019)

entries.name: Boddington
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained gold, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Bedrock resource almost 20 million troy ounces x 31.1035 g = 622 t (resource estimate, year not stated, excludes earlier production); reserves 390 t at end 2018, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Boddington Gold Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boddington_Gold_Mine : "A bedrock resource of almost 20 million troy ounces (620 million grams) was identified."; reserves "12.4 million troy ounces (390 tonnes) of gold" (31 December 2018)

entries.name: Lihir
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained gold, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Resource 46 million ounces x 31.1035 g = 1,431 t (year not stated, a resource figure, production not added), so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Lihir Island, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lihir_Island : "The mine holds one of the world's largest gold resources (46 million ounces (1.3 billion grams))."

entries.name: Cadia-Ridgeway
entries.source: Coordinate (near Orange, New South Wales) and contained gold from memory.

entries.name: Canadian Malartic
entries.source: Coordinate (Malartic, Quebec) and contained gold from memory; replaces malartic_gold, which was 0.5 degrees off.
entries.contained_basis: Proven and probable reserves 66.9 Mt at 1.11 g/t Au = 74.3 t gold (December 2019); production since 2011 not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Canadian Malartic gold mine, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/canadian-malartic-gold-mine/ : "66.9Mt of proven and probable" reserves "graded at 1.11 grams per ton" (December 2019)

entries.name: Cerro Rico de Potosi
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Total silver 1545-1800s about 30,000-60,000 t; range supplied by project owner and consistent with memory.
entries.contained_basis: Cumulative production 60,000 t silver + remaining reserves 1.76 billion ounces x 31.1035 g = 54,700 t (page states 50,000 tons) = 114,700 t; 'tons' taken as metric; years not stated on page
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Cerro Rico, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerro_Rico : "the Cerro Rico de Potosi mine to date has yielded an estimated 60,000 tons of silver"; "estimated reserves of 1.76 billion ounces (50,000 tons) of silver"

entries.name: Cannington
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production since 1997 at roughly a thousand tonnes of silver a year plus reserves, from memory. The earlier entry was two degrees west of the mine.
entries.contained_basis: June 2020 resources 79 Mt at 262 g/t Ag = 20,700 t silver (the same resource holds 6.2 Mt lead at 7.89% Pb); production since 1997 not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Mining Technology, Cannington silver-lead-zinc mine, https://www.mining-technology.com/projects/cannington/ : "79Mt at 262g/t Ag, 7.89% Pb and 5.36% Zn" (mineral resources, June 2020)

entries.name: Hamersley Province
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Pilbara iron ore, identified ore resource of order fifty billion tonnes at mid-fifties percent iron, from memory. fortescue_iron removed: it is a company working the same province.

entries.name: Carajas
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Reserves plus resources of order fifteen billion tonnes of ore at about two-thirds iron, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 18 Gt ore x 65.4% Fe = 11.77 Gt iron (year not stated; the page also gives 7.2 Gt resources, not combined); production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Carajas Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caraj%C3%A1s_Mine : "contains known reserves of 18 billion tons with an average grade of 65.4% Fe"

entries.name: Kiruna
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Original ore about two billion tonnes at roughly sixty percent iron, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Production since 1898 950 Mt ore x assumed 62.5% Fe (middle of the 60-65% the page gives for the 1985 reserves) = 594 Mt Fe, plus 2018 reserves 683 Mt ore x 43.8% Fe = 299 Mt Fe; total 893 Mt
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Kiruna Mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiruna_Mine : "Since mining began at the site in 1898, the mine has produced over 950 million tonnes of ore"; "As of 2018 the Kiruna Mine had Proven and Probable Reserves of 683 million tonnes grading 43.8% iron"; 1985 reserves "grading 60-65% iron"

entries.name: Sishen
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus reserves of order a billion tonnes of ore, from memory.

entries.name: Thabazimbi
entries.source: Coordinate from memory; no defensible endowment figure, omitted.

entries.name: Marcona
entries.source: Coordinate from memory; no defensible endowment figure, omitted.

entries.name: Norilsk-Talnakh
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained nickel, production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Measured and indicated nickel resources (include reserves) for the Norilsk and Talnakh deposits 11,778 kt at 31 December 2019; proven and probable reserves 6,176 kt; production not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Nornickel Annual Report 2019, Mineral resources and Ore Reserves, https://ar2019.nornickel.ru/en/appendices/resources-and-reserves.html : Taimyr Peninsula M&I resources nickel 11,778 kt, copper 22,167 kt (31 December 2019)

entries.name: Sudbury
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained nickel, production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory.
entries.contained_basis: USGS estimate that Sudbury contains about 19.8 Mt nickel in its sulphide deposits (as reported by The Northern Miner; year not stated, and whether it includes past production is not stated)
entries.contained_source: The Northern Miner, Treasure hunt - Sudbury: The Basin That Built a Mining Nation, https://www.northernminer.com/news/treasure-hunt-sudbury-the-basin-that-built-a-mining-nation/1003894370/ : "estimating that Sudbury contains about 19.8 million tonnes of nickel in its sulphide deposits"

entries.name: Bushveld Complex
entries.source: Bushveld holds the large majority of known platinum-group resources (USGS); figure from memory, coordinate is the complex centre (Rustenburg 25.67S 27.24E per Wikipedia). Earlier entry mislabelled the resource as nickel.
entries.contained_basis: Platinum-group elements plus gold resources and reserves of the Bushveld Complex about 72 kt (adapted from a USGS 2010 report on the page; platinum alone 38.1 kt); production not added
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Bushveld Igneous Complex, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushveld_Igneous_Complex : "The sum of PGEs and Gold resources and reserves equates to a total of about 72 kilotons from the Bushveld Complex alone."

entries.name: Broken Hill
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Original resource about three hundred million tonnes of ore at about ten percent lead; contained lead from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Through 1946, 63.8 million tons of ore had produced 8.6 million tons of lead (and 5.2 Mt zinc, 538 Moz silver = 16,700 t); ton type not stated and not converted; later production and remaining reserves not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Broken Hill ore deposit, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken_Hill_ore_deposit : "Through 1946, 63.8 million tons of ore have produced 8.6 million tons of lead, 5.2 million tons of zinc, 538 million ounces of silver"

entries.name: Mount Isa lead
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Contained lead, order of magnitude from memory. Renamed from mt_isa_pbzn.

entries.name: Viburnum Trend
entries.source: Southeast Missouri lead district; coordinate from memory (the earlier entry was half a degree off), contained lead order of magnitude from memory.

entries.name: Kinta Valley
entries.source: Perak, Malaysia; tin metal produced, order of magnitude from memory; coordinate from memory. kinta_underground_tin removed as a duplicate of this district.

entries.name: Bangka Island
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Tin metal produced since the 1700s, order of magnitude from memory.

entries.name: Olympic Dam uranium
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Resource of order two million tonnes of uranium, from memory.
entries.contained_basis: Reserves 2.95 Gt ore x 0.04% U = 1.18 Mt uranium (year not stated); production (about 4,000 t a year) not added, so a lower bound
entries.contained_source: Wikipedia, Olympic Dam mine, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Dam_mine : "estimated reserves of 2.95 billion tonnes of ore grading 1.2% copper, 0.04% uranium"

entries.name: Boke bauxite, Guinea
entries.source: Boke region coordinate from Wikipedia; Guinea holds the largest reserves in the world (USGS); regional figure from memory. Grade is kilograms of aluminium per tonne of ore. The earlier entry was 3.7 degrees east of Boke.

entries.name: Weipa
entries.source: Coordinate from Wikipedia. Production plus reserves, order of magnitude from memory. Renamed from australia_bauxite.
